title: Versioned event schema and projection commit seam
description: Objective: create the schema and transaction foundations that a projection/outbox subsystem needs, which the parent task could not reach from its own subtrees. SPIDR step 1 of 5, split from task-55d5a898264b4880a99bf2c5b3be120b after architect-c4babdf9 blocked it as unplannable. Deliverable: (a) a versioned SQLite migration adding projection, inbox, subscription, and cursor-generation tables that the exact-schema validator accepts as the new expected schema rather than rejecting as added objects; (b) a domain schema/canonicalizer version field on StoredEvent so later upcasters have something real to dispatch on; (c) a commit seam on EventLedgerStore letting a projection apply inside the existing BEGIN/write/COMMIT rather than after it. NOT in scope: the projection engine, upcasters, relay/inbox transaction logic, subscriptions, or CURSOR_GAP — those are steps 2-4 and must have somewhere to land, not be pre-empted here. Hard dependencies: none; task-9e3faf3b (SQLite schema decomposition, commit 9e16dde) already landed and split sqlite-schema.ts by conformance/integrity/migration/bootstrap — read that commit before planning, it is the seam you build against. Owned paths: packages/store/src/sqlite-schema*.ts, packages/store/src/event-ledger*.ts, packages/store/src/store-input*.ts only if the StoredEvent shape requires it, packages/store/src/index.ts for exports, and focused schema/migration/ledger tests. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: A forward migration adds projection, inbox, subscription, and cursor-generation tables, and the exact-schema validator accepts the migrated database as conformant rather than rejecting the added objects.
StoredEvent carries a domain schema/canonicalizer version that is written on append, read back unchanged, and is sufficient for a later upcaster to dispatch on without guessing.
EventLedgerStore exposes a commit seam that runs a caller-supplied apply step inside the same BEGIN/write/COMMIT as the event append, proven by a test where a failing apply rolls back the event.
Existing store tests pass unchanged, the focused store typecheck and test command exits 0, and only the explicitly owned paths are staged and committed.
taskRails: This task exists because the parent's ownership was too narrow. Do not repeat that error: if the plan needs a path not listed in Owned paths, say so in #architects before submitting rather than faking the capability.
Build the seam, not the feature. A projection engine, upcaster, relay, or subscription implemented here starves steps 2-4 and rebuilds the oversized task that was just split.
The exact-schema validator must be updated to expect the new tables, never weakened, bypassed, or made permissive about unknown objects.
Fail closed with stable reason codes; a failed apply inside the commit seam must roll back the event append, never leave a partial write.
Use TDD. Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400. Commit by explicit pathspec only.
reopenReason: Superseded — all three deliverables already landed under other tasks, verified in code, not just by task status. (a) projection/inbox/subscription/cursor tables: packages/store/src/sqlite-schema-manifest.ts via task-2d9b0a74 (DONE). (b) StoredEvent domain schema version: written on append at event-ledger-append.ts:177, read back at event-read-decode.ts:90, via task-a602b3d4 (DONE). (c) EventLedgerStore commit seam: applyWithinCommit at event-ledger-transaction.ts:124/129, same task. Planning this would have duplicated committed work. Note: projection steps 3-5 still cite it by title as a dependency; those references should resolve to task-2d9b0a74 + task-a602b3d4. Human delegated this call to governor on 2026-08-07.
